findings.claim: The repair silently deleted the `cites_no_such_six_item` guard: a reference to a §6 item that does not exist is now GREEN if it is written bare, so the mutation the case records as its own watched-red no longer reddens, and the 'Graded' half of §6 claims a property the code does not have.
findings.evidence: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED. src/browser/eval_adapter.py:688-695 — `slug` is group(3) of `_SIX_REF` and is None when no `(slug)` follows, so `slugs.get(n) != slug` becomes `None != None` -> False for any number the list does not have. Rewriting README.md:125 `§6 item 3 (same-ceiling) is why` to `§6 item 9 is why` returns `{'passed': True, 'wrong': []}` — I reproduced this. The old code emitted `{readme: cites_no_such_six_item, items: [9], list_is_1_to: 7}` for exactly this input, and published-band-matches-the-ledger.json:17 STILL records that output as watched-red; the key no longer exists anywhere in src/. ADR-019:189-193 says Graded = "every reference to this list ... names an item that exists AND spells its slug"; README.md:108-111 says "grades that each name points at the item it claims". Neither holds for a bare name.
findings.repro: rewrite README's `§6 item 3 (same-ceiling) is why` to `§6 item 9 is why` -> `_check_published_band()` returns passed True, wrong []
findings.acceptance: A reference whose number is outside 1..N is red whether or not it carries a slug (e.g. `if n not in slugs or slugs[n] != slug`). Watched red with the bare `§6 item 9` mutation, and the case's watched_red updated to the output the current code actually emits instead of the retired `cites_no_such_six_item` shape.

findings.claim: §6 item 8's stated property "each item opens with its slug" is not enforced for a trailing item: appending a slugless item 9 to §6 is invisible to both the 1..N check and the reference check.
findings.evidence: ORCHESTRATOR-VERIFIED. src/browser/eval_adapter.py:677-679 — `_SIX_ITEM` only matches lines that DO carry a slug, so a slugless item is simply absent from `slugs`; a gap in the middle is red, but a missing trailing item leaves `sorted(keys) == range(1, len+1)` intact. Appending `9. a brand new rule with no slug at all;` to §6 returns `{'passed': True, 'wrong': []}` — I reproduced this. Combined with R10, that new item can also be referenced bare and stay green. ADR-019:216-217 states this as graded.
findings.repro: append `9. a brand new rule with no slug at all;` to §6 -> passed True, wrong []
findings.acceptance: Numbered lines in §6 are enumerated independently of whether they carry a slug (match `^(\d+)\. ` first, then require the slug), so a slugless item is red. Watched red with the appended item 9.

findings.claim: The region-vacuity defect the implementer self-found is closed only for the one instance it hit — the region can still be silently truncated or widened by an ordinary edit, there is no non-vacuity guard, and the comment that claims otherwise is false in two of the three cases it names.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:681-686 — `region = here.split(_REGION[0],1)[1].split(_REGION[1],1)[0]`, with the comment at :682-684 asserting "Deleting the opening marker is an IndexError and deleting the closing one widens the region to the rest of the file — both loud, neither silently empty." (a) Deleting the closing marker is NOT loud: the only §6 reference outside the region is eval_adapter.py:3738 `§6 item 8 (references)`, which resolves, and there is no `property N` outside — result passed True. (b) Any comment inside the region that quotes the end-marker text truncates the region silently: inserting a comment naming the end marker above `_BAND_RATE` shrinks the region from 458 lines to ~20 and the check stays green — and it then MASKS a real defect: mis-pointing `# Item 4 (committed-ceiling).` to `# Item 4 (derivation).` is red with the region intact and GREEN with it truncated. Moving a band function below the end marker, or adding band code after it, is the same hole. No assertion on region size or content exists.
findings.repro: insert a comment quoting the end-marker text above `_BAND_RATE`, then mis-point `# Item 4 (committed-ceiling).` -> red with the region intact, green with it truncated
findings.acceptance: A non-vacuity guard on the region — e.g. red unless the region contains `def _check_published_band(` and `def _band_wrong(`, and both markers were found exactly once in the file — plus the comment corrected to say what is actually loud. Watched red by inserting a marker-quoting comment and by deleting the closing marker.

findings.claim: INDEX.md describes item 8's graded scope as "the check's own source" while ADR-019 and README both say "the marked band region" — and one §6 reference in that source file sits outside the graded region.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/INDEX.md:28 (ADR-019 row): "every reference to it — in that file, in README and in the check's own source — must name the item it points at, slug and all, or the gate is red". eval_adapter.py:3738 (`_run_doc_counts_case`) carries `§6 item 8 (references)`, outside the region (361-819) and therefore ungraded. It is correct today; it drifts silently on a renumber.

findings.acceptance: INDEX.md:28 says "the marked band region of the check's source", matching ADR-019:214-216 and README.md:110 — or the region grows to cover eval_adapter.py:3738.
